content:
maya: rolled driver v2.31 to green yesterday and we're seeing a p95 bump across small-seqlen jobs, KV hit rate dropped ~18% :thinking:

 dan: saw that in telemetry too. can you paste the perf profile? :eyes:

 maya: here are quick numbers from the first 2h after rollout vs canary:
 ```
 workload: chat-short (avg seq 32)
 canary: p50 42ms p95 120ms kv_hit 78%
 prod (post-rollout): p50 44ms p95 136ms kv_hit 60%
 regression ~13% p95
 ```

 sophia: interesting — kernel selector path looks different for short sequences; maybe fallback to slower matmul path when key lookup fails and we regen caches

 eli: any logs from the driver indicating key namespace change?

 maya: grep output from driver logs:
 ```
 INFO: cache-lease-manager: accepted namespace "model@abc123:v5" -> epoch=27
 WARN: cache-lookup: miss for key cache://model/abc123/ver5/seqbin-32/sha1=9f2a
 ```

 dan: aha, model version suffixing changed from "v5" to "ver5" in the driver metadata during the release. clients still write old prefix -> churn.

 sophia: that explains persisting hits dropping. we need an invalidation/compat handshake instead of full wipe. propose two-phase: 1) driver publishes new epoch + compat-mapping, 2) clients accept mapping and gradually rekey hot entries, 3) sweep old keys after TTL.

 maya: sketch of key format we want (backwards compat):
 ```
 key = "cache://model/{model_id}/meta/{epoch_id}/seqbin{b}/{kvhash}"
 // driver maintains alias list: aliases[old_namespace] -> epoch_id
 ```

 eli: operationally, we need atomic publish so routers know both aliases and canonical epoch. also add a "rekey_hint" header in responses so hot keys get rewritten on read.

 dan: rekey-on-read is my favorite. small pseudocode:
 ```
 if lookup(key_old) hit and epoch != current_epoch:
   write(key_new, value)
   return value
 ```

 sophia: two safety checks: limit rekey rate per-worker, and incremental sweep job that marks keys for deletion but doesn't delete until grace period.

 maya: rollout plan suggestion:
 - patch driver to emit alias map and bump epoch (canary)
 - client release with rekey-on-read + rate limit
 - monitor kv_hit, p95, and kernel path distribution
 - start sweep after 48h with exponential backoff

 runtime-bot: deployment-note: canary started @ 2310012000, prod started @ 2310012200, metric alerts: kv_hit_drop triggered at 2310012305

 eli: for metrics, we should add a trace tag to kernel-selector indicating "kv_miss_fallback" to quantify how often miss triggers slower path.

 dan: agree. added to infra backlog item #INF-849

 maya: next steps for today: maya will open PR with key-version aliasing proto, dan will draft client rekey patch, sophia will add selector trace tag. I'll coordinate canary -> prod rollback if numbers don't improve by EOD.

 sophia: one more note — ensure persistence layer retains both namespaces during upgrade; our s3-compatible compactor needs to be aware of aliases or we'll orphan objects.

 eli: good call. add compactor check to rollout checklist.

 maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
